description:

description:

A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges
An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country

And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you!

title: Scootin’ for Scoops with Strasburg Scooter Tours
location: Strasburg Scooter Tours, 246 N Decatur Street, Strasburg, 17579, United States
description:
Enjoy a 5-star Lancaster County ice cream tour experience with Strasburg Scooter Tours. You’ll see rolling farmlands, pass by horse and buggies, and enjoy some of the best Ice Cream in Lancaster County! It’s a stark contrast to the usual fast-paced and congested areas of larger cities. For those craving something different or one of the best romantic date night ideas, join us! 
We designed this tour to be an experience you can share with someone. We’ll only use Scoot Coupes, so single riders will have to look for someone to bring on the tour. It will be well worth it as you can expect exceptional views. Bond throughout the experience alongside our expert guide and relish some tasty ice cream* as we Ride around the rolling farmland surrounding the Village of Intercourse and Bird-in-Hand, PA.

An evening drive through PA Dutch Country

title: Fall Open House at Perfect Pots
location: Perfect Pots Greenhouse, 745 Strasburg Pike, Strasburg, PA, 17579, United States
description:
\Embrace the magic of the changing seasons at the Perfect Pots Fall Open House! Step into the Strasburg greenhouse to explore a vibrant selection of fall favorites—including bright celosia, colorful ornamental kale, and a huge variety of mums, all curated specifically for performance in container gardens. Guests can sip local apple cider and enjoy sweet seasonal treats while strolling through a greenhouse filled with inspiring autumn displays. 



During the visit, attendees can join an expert designer for a Fall Garden Trends Tour to get fresh ideas and easy planting “recipes” (registration is suggested, but not required). Plus, visitors can take advantage of the Complimentary Design Service by dropping off mid-sized summer pots for the team to transform into fall masterpieces. Don’t forget to spin the wheel at checkout, where everyone wins discounts, garden goodies, and more! Perfect Pots looks forward to hosting a day of cozy seasonal vibes and creative inspiration for all.

title: Root’s Old Mill Flea Market
location: Root’s Country Market and Auction, 705 Graystone Road, Manheim, PA, 17545, United States
description:
Come to Root’s Old Mill Flea Market and experience the thrill of discovering hidden treasures around every corner!
From vintage artwork and antique lamps to heirloom furniture and one-of-a-kind collectibles, you never know what you’ll find waiting for you at Root’s. 
Bring the whole family and enjoy browsing 175+ vendor stands offering a variety of antiques, collectibles, estate jewelry, household treasures, tools, decor, and so much more—indoors and outdoors.

*Please mention if you’re bringing a trailer or large vehicle, so that we may better accommodate you.

title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
location: Unique Lancaster, 23 N Walnut Street, Lancaster, 17603, United States
description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! 


Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. 


Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. 


But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. 


As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. 


Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. 


Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

description:

title: Evening Compline
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

This ride has been a classic in Lancaster County for a long time. The route is unique in that it starts and finishes at two different locations. As a result, most cyclists ride to the start and then ride home from the finish.

It starts at the Millersville Mart: 473 N George St, Millersville, PA 17551 (pictured) and the finish is at the new Bierhall Brewing Company: 1703 New Holland Pike, Lancaster, PA 17601. The Bierhall is open for lunch, so riders are welcome to stop in after the ride.

**This is a Challenging (A) level ride and intended to be a NO DROP RIDE.** The ride leader will ride at the advertised average speed and will do his/her best to keep the group together with regroupings and a sweeper may also be appointed at the start. **Please do not join this ride if you are not willing to stick with the group.** If maintaining an 18-20mph average is beyond your current ability level, please consider joining an "Advanced" ride first.

Helmets are mandatory. No earbuds. Please bring water and a basic repair kit (spare tube, tire levers, pump/CO2 inflator).

To eliminate passing around a pen and paper waiver, we require an LBC Club membership and Meetup RSVP below to join this ride.

Being on Meetup does not mean you are a club member. [Join here](https://www.lancasterbikeclub.net/content.aspx?page_id=60&club_id=257148).

Your RSVP is your agreement to abide by the club's [Code of Conduct](https://lancbikeclub.clubexpress.com/content.aspx?page_id=22&club_id=257148&module_id=323984),

[Rules of the Road](https://lancbikeclub.clubexpress.com/content.aspx?page_id=22&club_id=257148&module_id=325159), and [Ride Waiver](https://lancasterbikeclub.net/docs.ashx?id=454318)

description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. 
After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. 
The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. 
Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Evening Compline
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

Think you know the night? Think again. Behind the myths and "spooky" tropes lies one of the most efficient biological machines on the planet. Pennsylvania’s bats are tactical hunters, essential ecosystem anchors, and currently, they are fighting an uphill battle for survival.Join the Lancaster County Department of Parks & Recreation for an unfiltered look at the state of our skies. We’re moving past the basics to explore the high-stakes world of our six hibernating species and the seasonal migrators that cross our borders. We’ll discuss the grim reality of a 99% population collapse and the cascading effect that has on our local environment—specifically when it comes to controlling the world’s most prolific killer: the mosquito.From the bizarre evolutionary traits of bats across the globe to the specific conservation strategies needed right here in Lancaster County, this program is designed for those who want the real story. Come find out why these masters of the dark are the most important neighbors you’ve never met, and how you can play a role in their recovery 🦇

Jimmy Buffett often spoke of “traveling the songlines,” a phrase borrowed from the Aboriginal tradition of mapping the land through music and story—paths that connect people, places, and moments across time. 
Jammy Buffet picks up that journey, where Buffett’s coastal storytelling meets the improvisational spirit of the jam band world. 
Led by singer-songwriter Bob Barrick, with key contributions from Brendan Mayer (son of longtime Coral Reefer Band-member Peter Mayer), bassist Zeb Briskovich, drummer Tyler Gwynn, and multi-instrumentalist Mickey Lenny this Colorado–Tennessee outfit breathes new life into Buffett’s timeless “Gulf & Western” sound. 
Their live shows offer something for everyone: greatest-hit singalongs for casual fans, deep cuts for the diehard Parrotheads, and cosmic, exploratory jams for those along for the ride. Expect sun-soaked grooves, surprise segues, and barefoot boogie energy from start to finish. 
With collaborations featuring original Coral Reefers Roger Bartlett and Peter Mayer, Jammy Buffet is quickly making waves in the Gulf & Western world—bringing fresh musicianship and modern jam sensibilities to Buffett’s storied catalog.

description:

via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Entrepreneur, Reverend, Abolitionist: Stephen Smith’s Journey From Columbia to Philadelphia
location: LancasterHistory, 230 North President Ave, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17603, United States
description:
join LancasterHistory as they kick off the fall season of the Regional History Colloquium Series with speaker Michael Clemmons, who will discuss Entrepreneur, Reverend, Abolitionist: Stephen Smith’s Journey From Columbia to Philadelphia. Stephen Smith was a 19th-century African American raised in indentured servitude in Columbia, PA. He went on to become a leader in the African Methodist Episcopal Church, an advocate for freedom, and the richest Black man in America. Michael Clemmons, former Vice President of the Mother Bethel AME Church Historical Society, joins us to discuss the life of Stephen Smith, focusing on his accomplishments and setbacks in his journey from humble beginnings in Lancaster County to Philadelphia and Bethel AME Church.

title: W. Miller Barbour & His Prospect For Freedom
location: Lancsater Public Library, 151 N. Queen Street, Lancaster, 17603
description:
Join public historian Eric Schubert for a talk about a pioneering Pennsylvania human rights leader whose activism helped define mid-20th-century civil rights goals. This independent presentation explores Barbour’s remarkable journey from central Pennsylvania to the forefront of early civil rights activism and examines the enduring legacy of a forgotten champion for equality.Long before the modern Civil Rights Movement, W. Miller Barbour (1908–1957) dedicated his life to advancing racial equality and human rights. A Middletown native and Elizabethtown College graduate, Barbour rose from local roots to become a pioneering civil rights leader, serving with the Urban League in Denver and Los Angeles. Through advocacy, community organizing, and interracial dialogue, he expanded opportunities for African Americans decades before the landmark victories of the 1960s. 



 Eric Schubert is a public historian, genealogist, and forensic genetic genealogist as seen on Good Morning America and more. He serves on the Executive Committee of the Historic Preservation Trust of Lancaster County and is a White House Historical Association Next-Gen Leader. Schubert earned his M.A. in History at Millersville University. He was part of the research team which contributed to the award-winning documentary The Prospect for Freedom: W. Miller Barbour’s Human Rights Journey and independently organized the W. Miller Barbour Lecture Series alongside Abigail Sholes, which seeks to reintroduce Barbour’s legacy to communities across Pennsylvania.

title: "The Ballad of the Fugitive William Parker" Book Launch
location: The Stevens & Smith Center, 13-15 East Vine Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
LancasterHistory, in partnership with Pocket Books Shop, will host a book launch on Thursday, September 10, at The Stevens & Smith Center to celebrate the release of Cristin O’Keefe Aptowicz’s new book, The Ballad of the Fugitive William Parker. Aptowicz will sit down with local historian Darlene Colon to discuss the book’s importance and how it is the first narrative nonfiction account of the Christiana Resistance and the first to unite three of the radical abolitionist communities that made it possible. 
 (left) Local Historian, Darlene Colon, (right) Cristin O’Keefe Aptowicz, author of The Ballad of the Fugitive William Parker 
Cristin O’Keefe Aptowicz is the author of three nonfiction books and eight collections of poetry. Her forthcoming nonfiction book, The Ballad of the Fugitive William Parker, is the extraordinary forgotten story of an event known in its day as “the first shots of the Civil War”—a stylish, propulsive, intimately human tale of farmers, socialites, and self-emancipated folks with little in common who came together to stand against injustice… and won. 
Her previous nonfiction book, Dr Mutter’s Marvels: A True Tale of Intrigue and Innovation at the Dawn of Modern Medicine, spent three months on the New York Times bestseller list, and screenplays based on the book have won awards at the Philadelphia Film Festival, Hamptons International Film Festival, the Sloan Foundation, and the Black List. Her first nonfiction book, Words In Your Face: A Guided Tour Through Twenty Years of New York City, was named a “Poetry Book of the Year” by The Washington Post.

description:

The Ballad of the Fugitive William Parker is the first narrative nonfiction account of the Christiana Resistance, and the first to unite three of the radical abolitionist communities that made it possible: the wealthy free Black elite of Philadelphia, the rural white Quakers of Pennsylvania, and the fugitives from slavery who lived, worked, and ultimately fought in both worlds. title: Monthly Club Meeting - “Sparrows Simplified: Making Sense of LBJ’s”
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Michael Moore, retired Biology professor and past president of the Delaware Ornithological Society  
Many birders struggle with identifying sparrows, referring to them as LBJ’s (little brown jobs) or sparrow sp. This talk will help you tackle this difficult group. It will discuss and then attempt to blend the two main approaches to identification, the Peterson System and the Cape May School, to lead you to sparrow identification confidence. Each of the 16 species of regularly occurring sparrows in this area will be compared and contrasted with some discussion of finding and identifying rarities. 
Mike is a retired Biology Professor and a past president of the Delaware Ornithological Society. He started birding in middle school in Massachusetts and has had a life longpassion for birds. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington on the field endocrinology of White-crowned Sparrows. After doing a postdoc at the University of Texas in Austin, he served on the Biology Faculty at Arizona State University for 27 years.  He moved to the University of Delaware in in 2009 where he retired after 11 years. He has been funded throughout his career by the National Science Foundation and the Nation Institutes of Health and has published nearly 100 papers in scientific journals. He also has a passion for dragonflies and serves as a Vice President for the Dragonfly Society of the Americas.

Get The Led Out (GTLO) brings the thunderous power, mystique, and musical depth of Led Zeppelin to the stage in a high-energy live concert experience. This Philadelphia-based group of six seasoned musicians delivers Zeppelin’s legendary catalog with stunning precision—recreating the layered studio sound in ways even Zeppelin never performed live. If the record features three guitars, GTLO brings three guitars to the stage. The result is a massive, immersive wall of sound that stays true to the original recordings while feeling fresh and electrifying in concert. 
Dubbed “The American Led Zeppelin,” GTLO dives deep into the band’s iconic early years while also spotlighting fan-favorite deep cuts rarely heard live. The show also features a special acoustic set, highlighting the more intimate side of Zeppelin with songs like “Tangerine” and “Hey Hey What Can I Do.” 
With a strong national touring history and performances at major theaters and performing arts centers across the country, GTLO is known for delivering Zeppelin’s music with both power and nuance. No costumes, no gimmicks—just an honest, heart-pounding celebration of one of rock’s greatest catalogs. For longtime fans and new listeners alike, a GTLO show captures the light, shade, passion, and fury of “The Mighty Zep” in a truly unforgettable live experience.

title: ZZ Top: The Big One with special guest Jive Mother Mary
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $99 $119 $139 $159
 
ZZ Top Silver Premium Ticket Package  $309 
Package includes 

(1) Ticket located in the first 15 rows of the venue
Limited edition ZZ Top merchandise – exclusive to VIP packages

Rock legends ZZ Top have been delivering their signature blend of blues, boogie, and hard rock for over half a century. Formed in Houston in 1969 by Billy Gibbons, Dusty Hill, and Frank Beard, the band rose to national prominence with Tres Hombres and the enduring hit “La Grange,” before reaching global superstardom with 1983’s Eliminator and iconic tracks like “Sharp Dressed Man” and “Legs.” 
Famed for their unmistakable look—long beards, hot rods, and spinning guitars—ZZ Top became one of MTV’s defining acts while staying true to their deep blues roots. Their influences span legends like Muddy Waters, B.B. King, and Jimi Hendrix, shaping a sound that is both timeless and instantly recognizable. 
With millions of records sold, decades of worldwide touring, and an induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame by Keith Richards, ZZ Top remains one of the most enduring forces in rock. Following the passing of Dusty Hill, longtime guitar tech Elwood Francis stepped in on bass, helping carry the band’s legacy forward. 
Still going strong, ZZ Top continues to bring their trademark groove, grit, and swagger to audiences everywhere—driven by their enduring mantra: “Tone, Taste, and Tenacity.” 
Jive Mother Mary brings a soulful, hard-driving blend of Southern rock, blues, and classic rock to the stage. Known for powerful vocals, fiery guitar work, and high-energy live performances, the North Carolina-based band has shared the stage with artists including ZZ Top, Lynyrd Skynyrd, Foreigner, .38 Special, Blackberry Smoke, and Whiskey Myers. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: Indigenous Peoples and the American Revolution: The Sullivan Expedition of 1779
location: Historic Rock Ford, 881 ROCKFORD RD, Lancaster, 17602
description:
Historic Rock Ford’s Untold Stories of the American Revolution Lecture Series welcomes Mary Ann Levine as she presents “Indigenous Peoples and the American Revolution: The Sullivan Expedition of 1779.” 



In the late summer of 1779, under direct orders from George Washington, General John Sullivan led an army of several thousand men on a campaign against the Six Nations of the Haudenosaunee. The goal of the campaign was to break the confederacy’s ability to support and supply British forces by destroying food stores, burning villages, and driving the Haudenosaunee out of both Pennsylvania and New York. During the Sullivan expedition and its aftermath, an estimated 50%-60% of the Haudenosaunee died from direct military violence, disease, starvation, and exposure. In the early 20th century, dozens of memorials to the Sullivan campaign were erected over hundreds of miles of Sullivan’s march.  



This talk explores the Sullivan expedition, the memorialization of the campaign through commemorative markers in PA and NY, and the ways that Indigenous peoples are reframing the narrative around the campaign. This presentation will begin at 6:30 PM in the Langmuir Education Room on the first floor of the Rock Ford Barn. Please note that admission is for the lecture and does not include the Snyder Gallery.

description:

Unwind at the end of your day and join Gallery Grow for an intimate happy hour workshop with expert instruction. As always, BYOB. Slow down, connect with nature, and create your own living work of art.  



Kokedama, meaning “moss ball,” is a Japanese botanical art form that transforms a simple plant into a sculptural piece wrapped in living moss. During this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn the history behind Kokedama, create your own moss-covered plant design, and discover how to care for your new living companion. No experience necessary — just bring your creativity and a love for plants!

With a guitar slung over his shoulder and the amps turned up full tilt, Anthony Gomes electrifies blues and rock at a 21st century crossroads of his own. The Canadian vocalist, guitarist, songwriter and producer wails with all the force of a hurricane in the Mississippi Delta and enough fret-burning fireworks to leave his strings in flames. Over the years, he’s toppled the Billboard Blues Chart at #1, earned the endorsement of legends such as B.B. King, tallied tens of millions of streams, and packed shows on multiple continents. In 2026, Gomes is back supporting his #1 blues rock album, Praise the Loud, with a world tour that includes stops in 17 countries. 
“I’ve learned how to embrace my voice as a guitarist and as a singer,” he states. “I understand who I am, and I use my strengths to my advantage. I have a blues soul and a rock ‘n’ roll heart. I love to jump back and forth between both with a modern day approach. When I play rock, it’s got a little more dust on it.” 
​Born and raised in Toronto, Ontario, he fell in love with music as a kid, listening to everyone from Muddy Waters and Jimi Hendrix to Jeff Beck and Eddie Van Halen. At 14 years old, Anthony gravitated to the guitar and his relationship with the instrument was born. After grinding it out, his chops caught the attention of B.B. King’s bus driver at a jam night. Blown away, the driver introduced him to B.B. who invited him to open up a string of tour dates in 2005. Gaining invaluable knowledge from “The King,” he went on to share the stage with the likes of Buddy Guy, Robert Plant, Joe Bonamassa, Heart, Sammy Hagar, Kenny Wayne Shepherd, and more. Along the way, his concert attendees have included Academy® Award winner Morgan Freeman, John Goodman, and Vince Vaughn as well as Eric Clapton, to name a few.

The melody from The Doors’ “Hello, I Love You” laying atop Led Zeppelin’s “Misty Mountain Hop.” The pounding beat of Zep’s “When The Levee Breaks” coupled with the serene strumming of The Beatles’ “Dear Prudence.” The thematic sequence of The Rain Song – Riders On The Storm – Here Comes The Sun. These rare arrangements take crowds on an unexpected and exhilarating journey “Over The Hills And Far Away.” 
MMD also enhances the audience experience with a captivating visual presentation. Modern video screens and a stunning array of lighting allow this act to create an environment where the music comes to life. Fans young and old can “Break On Through” their daily distractions in this immersive and mesmerizing show.

title: Rhonda Vincent with The Malpass Brothers
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $39 $49 $69 
Rhonda Vincent is a powerhouse performer whose fiery talent and unmistakable voice have made her one of the most celebrated artists in bluegrass music. Hailing from Greentop, Missouri, Rhonda’s musical roots run five generations deep. She began performing professionally at just five years old with her family’s band, The Sally Mountain Show, gaining early experience on stage, radio, and television. By her teens, she had mastered multiple instruments and developed the work ethic and passion that would define her career. 
Her journey took a pivotal turn when a chance performance led to an invitation from the Grand Ole Opry—an early sign of the remarkable path ahead. Rhonda went on to build an award-winning career, earning the title “New Queen of Bluegrass” and becoming known for her signature blend of traditional roots and contemporary energy. Her breakthrough album Back Home Again cemented her status as a leading voice in the genre. 
A Grammy Award winner and one of the most decorated artists in bluegrass history, Rhonda Vincent has earned numerous honors, including multiple International Bluegrass Music Association Female Vocalist of the Year awards and Entertainer of the Year. In 2021, she achieved a lifelong dream with her official induction into the Grand Ole Opry. 
With a voice that transcends genres and collaborations that include artists like Dolly Parton, Rhonda Vincent continues to captivate audiences with high-energy performances, world-class musicianship, and a deep-rooted love of the music that started it all. 
As young boys, The Malpass Brothers – Christopher and Taylor – soaked up the music of their granddad’s phonograph records.  Christopher earned his first talent show trophy at age 7, and Taylor was playing mandolin by the time he was 10.  Today, they promote the work and music of classic country artists they treasure while creating new music and making their own mark in the lineage of a rich American cultural heritage.  With sincerity, honesty, and an utter ease on stage that belies their years, their smooth vocal blend and skillful musicianship layer infectiously into the deep respect they pay to legends who have paved the way.  Add the funny, off-the-cuff quips between the two 20-something siblings, and the engaging concert becomes a magnetic time-traveling journey to when a calmer rhythm reigned supreme.

description:
🌿 Pumpkin Succulent Planter Workshop 🎃 
Join us for a hands-on workshop where you’ll create a beautiful, long-lasting pumpkin succulent planter—a perfect centerpiece to brighten your space for months! 
What’s Included:  
✨ A real 6–7 lb. “Ghost” pumpkin
🌱 A variety of healthy succulents
🌾 Preserved moss and a mini bundle of dried florals
🪴 Soil and planting materials
📘 Step-by-step guided instruction from our experienced team 
We’ll teach you best practices for succulent care and maintenance—including soil and sunlight needs, watering, and propagation—so your plants thrive even after the season ends. 
💡 No carving or glue involved! That means your pumpkin stays fresh longer, and your succulents remain unharmed and easily transplantable when you’re ready to move them into a permanent home. 
🌟 Bonus: After you finish your pumpkin planter, we’ll also show you how to transfer your succulents into a long-term container so you can enjoy them for years to come!

**Todd Ritter - *Smart home automation without selling your soul to Big Tech***

At its core, true home automation is about shifting your living space from reactive to proactive, transforming a house full of isolated gadgets into a cohesive, intelligent ecosystem. Instead of juggling dozens of fragmented, vendor-locked cloud apps that stop working when the internet goes down, a locally-controlled platform like Home Assistant allows you to unify your hardware under one roof. Multiple Grammy® nominee Martina McBride has sold over 23 million albums to date, which includes 20 Top 10 singles and six #1 hits. 
Martina McBride has earned more than 15 major music awards, including four wins for Female Vocalist of the Year from the Country Music Association and won three Academy of Country Music for Top Female Vocalist. Martina has been awarded 14 Gold Records. Nine Platinum honors, three Double Platinum Records, and two Triple Platinum Awards. Martina was awarded the Covenant House Beacon of Hope Award and Music Business Association’s prestigious 2015 Harry Chapin Memorial Humanitarian Award for her philanthropic efforts on behalf of domestic violence. In 2019 Martina received the Cliffie Stone Icon Award at the ACM Honors event for her impactful contributions to Country Music.  Martina was honored during the 46th Annual Common Wealth Awards of Distinguished Service for her philanthropic work and contributions to society. In 2021 Martina unveiled her first exhibit in the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum, titled “The Power of Her Voice”. 
Martina has released two cookbooks – the first, Around the Table, a full-color illustrated collection of her favorite recipes, hosting tips, practical menu planning advice, and themed décor inspiration. title: American Disasters
location: Quarryville, QVL C.X. Carlson Cultural Room
description:
Discussion, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Best for adults and older interested teens. Registration is appreciated but not required if space allows.American Disasters is a six-session PowerPoint series. Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. Participants should prepare for lively presentations filled with interesting facts and peppered with humor. Dr. Frick’s goal is education with a smile.

Kenny G is the greatest-selling instrumental musician of the modern era and one of the best-selling artists of all time. With more than 75 million records sold worldwide and over 1.5 billion global streams, the Grammy Award–winning saxophonist has built a singular career spanning five decades of unprecedented success. His catalog includes some of the most iconic albums in music history, led by 1992’s Breathless—the best-selling instrumental album of all time—along with Duotones, Silhouette, Miracles: The Holiday Album, Heart and Soul, Brazilian Nights and most recently Innocence, his 20th studio album. 
Kenny G’s influence transcends jazz. He has embraced pop culture and his place in it, with humor, making surprise appearances across film, television, and major brand campaigns, collaborating with contemporary artists across genres, and maintaining a vibrant online presence that continues to resonate with new generations of fans. He published a memoir Life in the Key of G and is the subject of the HBO documentary Listening to Kenny G, both offering a candid, personal look at his life and legacy.

title: What Changed Your Mind?
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
What belief, assumption, or opinion have you genuinely changed your mind about—and what changed it?

Maybe it was religion, politics, science, morality, relationships, gender, economics, or something completely unexpected.
Each person will have a few minutes to tell the story of **one thing they once believed and no longer do**, and what evidence, experience, argument, or person caused the shift.

We’ll hear everyone first, without debate or interruption, then open the conversation.

This is not about proving who is right. It’s about something central to freethought: **being willing to reconsider what we think we know.**

Food and drinks available for individual purchase. Here's the menu: https://551west.com/menu/food/

**Attendance is limited to 8, including the organizer.**

title: The Knotwork Band Concert
location: Lititz, LTZ Community Room
description:
Music, Everyone

The Knotwork Band is a trio of musicians performing Celtic folk music, both traditional and modern. The band takes its name from Celtic knotwork, an art form particular to the ancient peoples of Ireland and Scotland where cords or lines are woven into intricate patterns and highly stylized designs. Like Celtic knotwork, the talents of the individual members are interwoven to form each piece of music.The audience can expect to hear Celtic folk music from Ireland, Scotland, England, and Brittany, as well as American and World music with ties to Celtic folk music, either musically or historically. Their wide spectrum of musical styles ranges from beautiful waltzes to exciting jigs and reels. The band’s music ranges from slow and hauntingly beautiful melodies to faster-paced and energetic pieces which will get the toes tapping. Our September concert will be a memorial concert in honor of William H. Sweger. Bill was a member of the Lititz Public Library’s Board of Trustees for 12 years and during that time held the offices of Secretary, Vice President and President. He joined the Board during the exciting years that led to the construction of the current library facility. Please join us for this memorial concert in his honor.

title: Storm Science: The Real Meteorology Behind the Movies
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Presentation, STEM, Virtual, Adults, Seniors

Are you fascinated by the sheer power of extreme weather? ⚡ Ever wondered how much of Hollywood’s natural disaster movies is actually based on real science? 🎬Join us at the library for a special virtual presentation with Kyle Elliott, Director of the Weather Information Center at Millersville University, for an inside look at the wild world of meteorology! Kyle will be joining us live via Zoom on our big screen to dive deep into the science of our atmosphere.Designed specifically for adults who love to know how things work, this program will cover:🚗 Storm Chasing & Field Research: What it’s actually like to pursue severe thunderstorms and tornadoes in the field to study extreme conditions.🔮 Weather Forecasting: How meteorologists predict major weather events before they hit.❄️ Local Winter Storms: A look into the powerful winter weather systems that shape our local climate.🚨 Weather Safety: Understanding the critical differences between weather watches and warnings to keep you weather-ready.Bring your curiosity for a live Q&A session with Kyle following the presentation! 🗣️❓🎟️ Registration is recommended to ensure your seat in the room. Sign up today!

Every decision you make has consequences.... both good & bad depending on the Jenga tower. location: Lancaster, LPL Board Room

The book combines data-driven and metaphysical approaches. Ages 18+ · Space is limited · Registration required

Renowned as one of the greatest violinists of all time, Itzhak Perlman brings extraordinary artistry, warmth, and joy to audiences around the world. A true icon of classical music, Perlman has performed with every major orchestra and in the world’s most celebrated concert halls, earning 16 GRAMMY® Awards, multiple Emmy Awards, a Kennedy Center Honor, and the Presidential Medal of Freedom. 
In addition to his celebrated orchestral appearances, Perlman continues to captivate audiences through special programs and intimate recitals alongside longtime collaborator Rohan De Silva. A passionate advocate for music education, he and his wife Toby founded the Perlman Music Program, helping to mentor and inspire the next generation of musicians.

A longtime collaborator of Itzhak Perlman, De Silva brings a refined musical partnership that enhances every performance with nuance and balance. His artistry has been praised for its elegance and versatility, seamlessly supporting and elevating the soloist while shining in his own right. 
Together, De Silva and Perlman create an extraordinary concert experience, blending technical mastery with heartfelt musical connection.

Country music trailblazers Diamond Rio have been delivering chart-topping hits and signature harmonies for decades. Formed in the late 1980s, the band made history with their debut single “Meet in the Middle,” becoming the first country group ever to reach No. 1 with a debut release. They quickly followed with a string of hits, including “How Your Love Makes Me Feel,” “One More Day,” “Beautiful Mess,” “Unbelievable,” and “I Believe,” earning a reputation for their rich vocals and exceptional musicianship. 
With more than 6.8 million albums sold, over a billion global streams, and an impressive run of 20 Top 10 singles, Diamond Rio has remained a constant force in country music. Known for playing every note on their recordings, the band’s artistry extends beyond radio hits to acclaimed instrumental performances and genre-spanning projects, including their Grammy Award-winning Christian album, The Reason. 
A member of the Grand Ole Opry and recipient of multiple CMA, ACM, and Grammy honors, Diamond Rio continues to captivate audiences with their timeless sound and energetic live performances. Don’t miss your chance to experience one of country music’s most celebrated groups live in concert.

title: America250PA: Revolution to Reconstruction: Pennsylvania and the Fight for Liberty & Equality
location: The Ware Center for the Performing Arts, 42 N. Prince Street, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Clint Smith
Join LancasterHistory on October 7 as we welcome award-winning author Clint Smith for “Revolution to Reconstruction: Pennsylvania and the Fight for Liberty & Equality,” an America250PA lecture. Smith will share insights on Pennsylvania’s central role in shaping our ideals of liberty & equality from the Revolution through Reconstruction and the notion that there is no such thing as a single American story. 
Clint Smith is the author of the upcoming nonfiction book, Just Beneath the Soil (Knopf, May 2027) which explores how World War II is remembered around the world. He is also wrote the narrative nonfiction book, How the Word Is Passed: A Reckoning With the History of Slavery Across America, which was a #1 New York Times bestseller, winner of the National Book Critics Circle Award for Nonfiction, the Hillman Prize for Book Journalism, the Stowe Prize, and selected by the New York Times as one of the 10 best books of 2021. With Sonja Cherry-Paul, Smith adapted How the Word Is Passed into a bestseller for young readers (Little, Brown, 2025). He is also the author of the New York Times bestselling poetry collection Above Ground and the award-winning poetry collection Counting Descent. His writing has been published in The New Yorker, The New York Times Magazine, Poetry Magazine, The Paris Review, and elsewhere. In 2020, Smith was named a New America (Emerson Collective) Fellow, and in 2026 was named the inaugural fellow of the Sachs Foundation. Clint received his B.A. in English from Davidson College and a Ph.D. in Education from Harvard University. He is a staff writer at The Atlantic. 
EVENT DETAILS & HOW TO REGISTER 
The event, “Revolution to Reconstruction,” will take place on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at the Ware Center for the Performing Arts, 42 N. Prince Street in Lancaster, PA. Doors open at 5pm, followed by the lecture at 5:30pm. Tickets are free, but registration in advance is required as capacity is limited and this event is anticipated to sell out. The event will include a Q&A portion for our audience, and will not be livestreamed or recorded. 
To register, please click the link below or call 717.392.4633 to book over the phone. 
REGISTER FOR OCTOBER 7 
Signed copies of Clint Smith’s How the Word Is Passed will be available for purchase on-site, thanks to our friends at Pocket Books Shop on Prince! Cash and card are accepted. 

Thank You to America250PA for Their Support of This Event!

Her books have been translated into over twenty languages, picked for Book of the Month Club, awarded the RITA, Booksellers Best, and Golden Leaf awards, and chosen for the American Library Association’s annual list of the best genre fiction. title: Freethought Walking Salon: How Do We Build Community Without Church?
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
Churches have long provided more than religion: friendship, practical help, ritual, belonging, and people who show up when life gets hard.
What could a freethought community provide instead?

### Route

* **Meet:** north-east side of Penn Square, on E. King St.
* **Blazin’ J’s, 15 E King St** — savory bite
* **Aura Little Cafe, 44 N Queen St** — coffee, tea, or light snack
* **Ewell Plaza/Binns Park, 123 N Queen St** — main seated discussion stop
* **Lancaster Sweet Shoppe, 141 N Duke St** — dessert finish

Total walking is roughly **0.7 mile**.

### Questions

* What do people actually get from church communities besides religion?
* What kind of support should LFS provide when someone is sick, lonely, grieving, moving, or simply needs company?
* What recurring rituals or gatherings could create belonging without becoming church-like?
* **Closing:** What would make LFS feel like your community, not just a Meetup group?

Food and drinks are purchased individually.

**Parking:** Penn Square Garage, 28 S Duke St, approximately a 2–3 minute walk from our meeting point.
**Weather:** postponed if rain or unpleasant walking conditions are expected.

title: The Statler Experience
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $24 $34 $44
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, March 4 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, March 6 at 10:00 a.m. 








The Statler Experience brings the timeless harmonies of The Statler Brothers back to the stage in a heartfelt celebration featuring the next generation of Statler family talent: Wilson Fairchild (Wil & Langdon Reid) and Jack and Davis Reid. 
As sons and grandsons of original Statler Brothers members, these artists carry not only the sound — but the spirit — of one of country music’s most beloved vocal groups. Audiences will hear classic hits like “Flowers on the Wall,” “Bed of Rose’s,” “Do You Remember These,” and “Elizabeth,” delivered with the rich harmonies, warmth, and authenticity that defined the original quartet. 
Beyond the music, The Statler Experience offers personal stories, humor, and behind-the-scenes memories that connect generations of fans to the heart of the Statler legacy. It’s more than a tribute — it’s a family tradition brought to life on stage. 
If you cherish classic country, tight harmonies, and songs that stand the test of time, this is an evening you won’t want to miss. 








For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

Busy BabiesA Baby & Caregiver Class for Ages 6–17 MonthsCome sing, play, and grow together! Busy Babies is a playful, hands-on class designed for babies ages 6–17 months and their caregivers. title: Ghosts, Monsters, and Tales of Adventure with Uncharted Lancaster
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Are you brave enough to explore the haunted corners of Lancaster County? Join Uncharted Lancaster founder and local historian Adam Zurn for an evening of eerie legends, mysterious happenings, and true tales of the unexplained. This event promises a thrilling blend of history and the supernatural that will leave you glancing over your shoulder on the walk back to your car. From battlefields to backroads, Lancaster County’s long history hides more than a few restless spirits. In the Ghosts, Monsters, and Tales of Adventure presentation, Adam shares some of his favorite stories from his recent book of the same name. The presentation combines historical research, eyewitness accounts, and local folklore to reveal how the past still echoes through the present.Prepare to meet long-dead soldiers, vengeful spirits, and mysterious creatures that haunt the river valleys and hollow hills of the Susquehanna region. Some stories may chill your bones, while others will spark your sense of wonder at just how deep Lancaster’s legends run.

location: Lititz, LTZ Community Room

Yiddish Book CenterThe Golem: How He Came into the World (Der Golem, wie er in die Welt kam, 1920) is a German silent horror film directed by Paul Wegener (with Carl Boese) and co-written by Henrik Galeen, based on Gustav Meyrink’s 1915 novel.  It is considered a leading example of early German Expressionism and is notable for being the only surviving film in a trilogy of golem-themed works by Wegener.The movie runs 1 hour and 15 minutes. Popcorn and soda will be served.

description:

Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. Participants should prepare for lively presentations filled with interesting facts and peppered with humor. Dr. Frick’s goal is education with a smile.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 21, 2026
Feed your mind and delight your palate as you visit local Lancaster County farms, learn about their unique operations and sample the fruits of their labors. John Smucker is your host for this tour, which includes a flavorful luncheon featuring fresh, locally grown foods. It’s the ultimate farm-to-fork experience! 
Includes:

Two-night stay in the historic Bird-in-Hand Village Inn & Suites
Tour of local farms and a lunch made with ingredients from our tour – see itinerary below
Daily deluxe continental breakfast for two at the Village Inn & Suites or credit at the Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe
Dinner for two at the Bird-in-Hand Family Restaurant & Smorgasbord on Tuesday or Wednesday
Welcome market basket filled with local foods
Homemade pumpkin pie from the Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe

Space is limited so reserve early. Enjoy this package for $595 (plus tax). Extend your stay for only $119 a night (plus tax). 
Call (800) 914-2473 to reserve your stay. For more information on the Village Inn & Suites, click here. Walking is required for these tours. 
Requires $200 deposit to reserve your tour (refundable up to two weeks prior to event). $119 extra night available for any room type. Taxes not included. 
Empty heading
Tour Stops:
5:30 am  Rise, Shine & Dine:  Wake up with the roosters and see cows being milked at our neighbor Aaron Lantz’s organic farm. Then savor a delicious farm-fresh breakfast with the Lantz family in their kitchen. 
7:30 am  The Time is Ripe: Take an orchard tour of Kauffman’s Fruit & Farm Market and learn how they produce their apple butter and apple cider. 
9:15 am  Goats on the Farm: Amish farmer Amos Miller at Misty Creek Goat Dairy will demonstrate how to make goat cheese. Shop in his store on the farm for goat’s milk soaps and lotions before you leave. 
11:00 am  Hydroponic Farming: At Millcreek Hydroponics, we’ll learn about the sustainable year-round growing methods for their lettuce and microgreens, and tour their greenhouse. 
12:00 pm  Grown Local Luncheon: You’ve seen where it’s grown. Now taste the farm-fresh difference. Receive a market basket of local foods after lunch. 
1:00 pm   Perfectly Pumpkin: Our last stop after lunch will be a visit to Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe. See how we make our famous pies with home-grown pumpkins and take one home. You can even try our handcrafted Pumpkin Gingersnap artisan ice cream.

title: Screening of the documentary Welcome To Yiddishland
location: Lititz, LTZ Community Room
description:
Movie & Film, Adults, Seniors

Welcome to Yiddishland offers an upbeat, witty and timely exploration of this international community of artists, who are rediscovering and revitalising Yiddish culture. Whilst being a highly entertaining Arts film, full of joyous music, and performances; it also reframes our understanding of Jewish culture and identity.The film is timely in that it breaks down the current reductionist stereotyping of Jews that allow anti-Semitic hate to fester and constructive discourse to suffocate. It probes the nuanced aspects of Jewish culture and identity to reveal the multi-layered aspects of what it means to identify as Jewish and engage in Jewish culture.Through intimate interviews and rare behind-the-scenes access to some of the world's top musicians and performers working in Yiddish, we showcase the innovative works of artists who use this ancient language as a vehicle for addressing contemporary issues such as Queer identity, the refugee crisis, war and authoritarianism.This community is not large in overall numbers but they are global, spreading from Mexico and Buenos Aires, Berlin, New York, Paris, Melbourne and more.They are having a big impact. Indeed they are driving a renaissance in Yiddish Arts and Culture.Film runs 1 hour and 35 minutes.

Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. description:

Whether you’re a die-hard bluegrass fan or simply looking for a night of great live music, Hammer Creek delivers the timeless songs of simpler days. Their music takes you back to the roots of bluegrass, honoring legendary pioneers like Flatt & Scruggs, The Stanley Brothers and Bill Monroe. With driving banjo, heartfelt harmonies, and that unmistakable high lonesome sound, they bring this traditional American musical genre to life one song at a time. 
Based in Lancaster County, Hammer Creek was formed in 2020 and have played shows throughout Pennsylvania, Maryland and surrounding areas, including the Buck Moon Bluegrass Festival, the Appalachian Trail Music Festival and Fort Hunter Days. They have thrice been nominated for the Central Pennsylvania Music Award as Best Bluegrass Band. 
Join us for a wholesome evening of traditional tunes and masterful musicianship.

title: The Treachery of Botany: Poisonous Garden Plants
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Discussion, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

🌿 BEAUTY OR BANE? THE SECRET LIFE OF YOUR GARDEN 💀Vibrant lavender and mauve blossoms sway in the breeze while butterflies dip and dance above. With every rustle of foliage, delicate white buds flash in the sunlight. It’s the ultimate dream landscape—an idyllic, peaceful sanctuary designed for pure relaxation.But look closer. Hidden within this botanical paradise, unexpected danger might be lurking right in plain sight.Is that vivid red berry harmless or a hazard?What secret is that unusual violet flower stalk hiding?Could your pet's favorite sunbathing spot be surrounded by toxic greenery?Uncover the truth behind the beauty! Join speakers Cynthia Trussell, Indigo Bowser, and Kathy Vu of the Penn State Master Gardeners for The Treachery of Botany: Poisonous Garden Plants. In this eye-opening 45-minute presentation (followed by a Q&A session), you'll learn how to identify ordinary, uncommon, cultivated, and wild poisonous plants in your landscape-- discover what makes them tick, and master easy, practical ways to manage them safely.Keep your loved ones safe while keeping your sanctuary gorgeous. Don't miss it-- turn your garden into a true, worry-free paradise!

Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

Medicare Annual Open Enrollment Appointments at Quarryville LibraryLancaster County Office of Aging runs a program called PA Medi, formerly APPRISE. This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. Insurance changes made during the Open Enrollment time become effective January 1, 2027.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)
source: Meetup: The Creative House of Lancaster

Join us to discover the secret history of these iconic structures and see how they continue to shape our landscape today.

Medicare Annual Open Enrollment Appointments at Quarryville LibraryLancaster County Office of Aging runs a program called PA Medi, formerly APPRISE. This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. Insurance changes made during the Open Enrollment time become effective January 1, 2027.

title: Understanding Immigration Law: Asylum
location: Quarryville, QVL C.X. Carlson Cultural Room
description:

Registration is preferred; walk-ins will be accommodated as space allows. Best for adults and older interested teens.We welcome local immigration attorney Paige Britton, who will share her professional experience working within the U.S. immigration system over several sessions, exploring a different element each month.Asylum – How can a person gain safety from persecution?Learn about the laws that offer protection to noncitizens fleeing harm in their home countries. How easy is it to get asylum, and who qualifies? What do they need to prove, and how do they make their case for asylum relief? The group is known for its lively, thoughtful discussions and makes a concerted effort to respect differing viewpoints. To keep conversations focused and meaningful, social chatter, gossip, and romance novels are generally kept outside the allotted discussion time.Lit Lovers gravitate toward modern fiction distinguished by strong writing, well-developed characters, and compelling narratives. title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)
source: Meetup: The Creative House of Lancaster

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.

title: Night Shift at Lancaster Science Factory
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Night Shift 2026-27  
Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. New to this year, educators will be leading hands-on STEM workshops in our Maker Space! Consider joining us for the Night Shift with your scout group, sports team or even for a special birthday!  
Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.   
Dates:  
Saturday, November 7-Sunday, November 8, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, December 5-Sunday, December 6, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, February 13-Sunday, February 14, 2027  

Click here to register 

Saturday, April 17-Sunday, April 18, 2027  

Click here to register 

Itinerary:  

6:30-7:00 pm: Arrival, check in 


7:00-10:00 pm: Museum exploration, Science Cafe activity, scavenger hunts, workshops 


7:15-7:55: Group A workshop 


8:05-8:45: Group B workshop 


8:55-9:25: Group C workshop 


10:00-10:30 pm: Set up sleeping accommodations 


10:30 pm: Get ready for lights out 


7:00-8:00 am: Light breakfast available 


8:30 am: Exhibit hall closes

title: Girl Scout Badge Workshops (Robotics)
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Badge Workshops for Daisies through Juniors
The Lancaster Science Factory is pleased to offer an expanded menu of Girl Scout workshops designed to educate, challenge, and empower scouts while completing badge requirements. 
Workshops are 1 hour unless otherwise noted. Register a single scout or the whole troop for upcoming workshops listed below. 
  
Robotics Badge Workshops
Learn all about robotics with our hands-on Robotics Badge workshops! All workshops cover the Robotics Badge 1 for each troop level. 
Robotics workshops will be offered on the following dates: 
Saturday, October 17, 2026
–Daisies and Brownies from 1:30-2:30 pm (register here) 
–Juniors from 3-4 pm (register here) 
Saturday, December 12, 2026
–Daisies and Brownies from 1:30-2:30 pm (register here) 
–Juniors from 3-4 pm (register here) 
Saturday, March 20, 2027
–Daisies and Brownies from 1:30-2:30 pm (register here) 
–Juniors from 3-4 pm (register here) 
  
Can’t make it to a scheduled workshop? Reach out to Megan Stoltzfus at mstoltzfus@tlsf.org to schedule a private workshop. Availability is limited for private workshops, so we recommend scheduling ahead by a minimum of 1-2 months if possible.
Program attendance, cancellation, and refund policy.

Cancellations (by the registrant) received less than one week prior to the workshop will be subject to a refund of 1/2 of the total registration cost for that workshop. Cancellations received prior to that shall receive a full refund.
Workshops canceled by the Lancaster Science Factory for ANY reason will be refunded fully.

title: Night Shift at Lancaster Science Factory
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Night Shift 2026-27  
Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. New to this year, educators will be leading hands-on STEM workshops in our Maker Space! Consider joining us for the Night Shift with your scout group, sports team or even for a special birthday!  
Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.   
Dates:  
Saturday, November 7-Sunday, November 8, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, December 5-Sunday, December 6, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, February 13-Sunday, February 14, 2027  

Click here to register 

Saturday, April 17-Sunday, April 18, 2027  

Click here to register 

Itinerary:  

6:30-7:00 pm: Arrival, check in 


7:00-10:00 pm: Museum exploration, Science Cafe activity, scavenger hunts, workshops 


7:15-7:55: Group A workshop 


8:05-8:45: Group B workshop 


8:55-9:25: Group C workshop 


10:00-10:30 pm: Set up sleeping accommodations 


10:30 pm: Get ready for lights out 


7:00-8:00 am: Light breakfast available 


8:30 am: Exhibit hall closes 

Questions? Reach out to mstoltzfus@tlsf.org
